definition_en: the systematic study of the physical world, the knowledge gained from it, or a particular field of such study

scene: 他翻开课本，想弄明白实验背后的道理。Science explains how the experiment works.

senses.title: Systematic knowledge
senses.definition: the organized study of the physical world through observation and experiment
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察和实验对物质世界进行的有系统研究
senses.example: Science has changed daily life.
senses.why: The central sense is organized knowledge of nature.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是关于自然的有组织知识。

senses.title: Scientific activity
senses.definition: the work of doing scientific research

senses.example: Science needs patience and honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 科学研究需要耐心与诚实。
senses.why: The knowledge sense extends to the activity that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 知识义延伸到产生知识的研究活动。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: a particular branch of systematic study
senses.definitionCN: 系统研究的某个分支
senses.example: She studies computer science.
senses.why: A broad method narrows to one named discipline.
senses.whyCN: 宽泛的方法缩小为一个具体学科。

intro.en: Science comes from Latin scientia, knowledge, from scire, to know.
intro.cn: science 源自拉丁语 scientia（知识），来自 scire（知道）。

items.en: Scire meant to know.
items.cn: scire 意为知道。

items.en: Scientia meant knowledge or understanding.
items.cn: scientia 意为知识或理解。

items.en: Science meant knowledge of any kind.
items.cn: science 意为任何类型的知识。

items.en: Science narrowed to knowledge based on observation.
items.cn: science 缩小为基于观察的知识。

items.en: Science now names the study of the natural world.
items.cn: 现代英语中 science 指对自然世界的研究。

note.en: Science is compared with similar-looking words and with words for knowledge and study.
note.cn: 把 science 与形近词以及表示知识与研究的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sense of right and wrong

normalIntro.en: Science is knowledge, scientific is the adjective, and scientist is the person.
normalIntro.cn: science 是知识，scientific 是形容词，scientist 是人。

normal.en: Science fiction mixes science with imagination.
normal.cn: 科幻小说把科学与想象结合。

normal.en: Computer science is the study of computing.
normal.cn: 计算机科学是研究计算的学科。

normal.en: A science lab is where experiments happen.
normal.cn: 科学实验室是做实验的地方。

normal.en: Science and scientist share the same base.
normal.cn: science 与 scientist 同根。

normal.en: The ence ending marks a noun.
normal.cn: ence 结尾提示这是名词。

abstract.en: Science began as knowledge in general, then narrowed to tested knowledge.
abstract.cn: science 起初泛指知识，后来缩小为经过检验的知识。

abstract.en: The word links a method, a body of knowledge, and a field.
abstract.cn: 这个词连接方法、知识体系与学科。

abstract.en: To know is the heart of science.
abstract.cn: 「知道」是 science 的核心。

examples.en: Science has changed daily life.
She studies computer science.
The science of medicine grows fast.

dict_mnemonic.text: science 源自拉丁语 scire（知道），ence 构成名词，所以 science 就是「系统化的知识」。

root: 源自拉丁语 scientia（知识），来自 scire（知道），核心义「经系统研究获得的知识」。

sensesIntro.en: Science means systematic knowledge, the activity of research, or a particular field of study.
sensesIntro.cn: science 意为系统知识、研究活动，或某个学科。

core.en: Knowledge built by observation and testing.
core.cn: 通过观察与检验建立的知识。

branches.en: Organized knowledge of nature.
branches.cn: 关于自然的有组织知识。

branches.en: The work of testing and discovering.
branches.cn: 检验与发现的工作。

branches.en: One named branch such as chemistry.
branches.cn: 像化学这样的具体学科。

branches.en: Knowledge and research depend on each other.
branches.cn: 知识与研究相互依存。

branches.en: Each discipline has its own methods.
branches.cn: 每个学科都有自己的方法。

intro.en: Science forms words for its method, people, and fields.
intro.cn: science 构成表示方法、人物与学科的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin scientia and scire are the sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scientia 与 scire 是词源。

科学家们分享研究结果。
这个说法经过了科学检验。
计算机科学吸引许多学生。

items.meaning: the study of people and society
items.exampleCN: 社会科学研究人类群体。

definition_zh: 科学的；科学研究的；严谨系统的
definition_en: relating to science or its methods, or careful and systematic in approach
core_image: 研究者戴着护目镜，把样本放进仪器，旁边的记录表写得整整齐齐
scene: 研究团队用科学的方法检验这个说法。The team used a scientific method to test the claim.
sceneCN: 这里 scientific 是「科学的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：研究团队用科学的方法检验这个说法。

senses.title: Relating to science
senses.definition: connected with science or the work of scientists
senses.definitionCN: 与科学或科学家的工作有关的
senses.example: They need scientific evidence.
senses.why: The main sense points to the field of science.
senses.whyCN: 主要义项指向科学领域。

senses.title: Careful and systematic
senses.definition: done in a careful, organized, and testable way
senses.definitionCN: 以谨慎、有条理且可检验的方式进行的
senses.example: Her approach is scientific and careful.
senses.why: The method of science becomes a general style of thinking.
senses.whyCN: 科学方法变成一种普遍的思维方式。

senses.title: Used in science
senses.definition: designed or used for scientific work
senses.definitionCN: 为科学工作设计或使用的
senses.example: The lab bought scientific instruments.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室购买了科学仪器。
senses.why: Objects and tools take the label of the field they serve.
senses.whyCN: 物品与工具以所服务领域的名称来命名。

intro.en: Scientific combines Latin scientia, knowledge, with the ending fic, making.
intro.cn: scientific 由拉丁语 scientia（知识）与表示「造成」的结尾 fic 组合而成。

items.en: Scientia meant knowledge.
items.cn: scientia 意为知识。

items.en: Scientificus meant producing knowledge.
items.cn: scientificus 意为产生知识的。

items.en: Scientific entered English meaning producing knowledge.
items.cn: scientific 进入英语时意为产生知识的。

items.en: It came to mean relating to science.
items.cn: 它开始表示与科学有关的。

items.en: Scientific also means systematic and careful.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scientific 还表示系统严谨的。

note.en: Scientific is compared with related forms and with adjectives for careful inquiry.
note.cn: 把 scientific 与相关词形以及表示严谨探究的形容词作比较。

entries.definition: done according to a clear plan

normalIntro.en: Scientific is the adjective of science, formed with the ending fic.
normalIntro.cn: scientific 是 science 的形容词，由结尾 fic 构成。

normal.en: Scientific method is a careful way to test ideas.
normal.cn: 科学方法是检验想法的严谨方式。

normal.en: Scientific evidence supports a claim.
normal.cn: 科学证据支持某个说法。

normal.en: The scientific community shares results.
normal.cn: 科学界共享研究结果。

normal.en: Unscientific means not based on science.
normal.cn: unscientific 意为不科学的。

normal.en: Scientific and science share the sci base.
normal.cn: scientific 与 science 共享 sci 词干。

abstract.en: The ending fic means making, so scientific once meant knowledge-making.
abstract.cn: 结尾 fic 意为造成，因此 scientific 原意为「产生知识的」。

abstract.en: Science as a method becomes an adjective for any careful work.
abstract.cn: 科学作为一种方法，其形容词可形容任何严谨工作。

abstract.en: To call work scientific is to demand evidence.
abstract.cn: 称一项工作为科学的，就是要求证据。

examples.en: They need scientific evidence.
The claim has no scientific basis.
examples.cn: 这个说法没有科学依据。

examples.en: The lab bought scientific instruments.
examples.cn: 实验室购买了科学仪器。

dict_mnemonic.text: science 是「知识、科学」，fic 表示「产生……的」，scientific 就是「产生科学知识的、科学的」。

root: 由 science（科学）加后缀 fic（产生……的）构成，远源为拉丁语 scientia（知识）与 facere（做）。

sensesIntro.en: Scientific means relating to science, careful and systematic, or used for scientific work.
sensesIntro.cn: scientific 意为与科学有关的、严谨系统的，或用于科学工作的。

core.en: Marked by the methods and standards of science.
core.cn: 具有科学方法与标准的。

branches.en: Connected with the field of science.
branches.cn: 与科学领域相关。

branches.en: Done with care, order, and tests.
branches.cn: 以谨慎、条理与检验完成。

branches.en: Tools made for research work.
branches.cn: 为研究工作制造的器具。

branches.en: The field and its method reinforce each other.
branches.cn: 领域与方法相互强化。

branches.en: Instruments serve careful inquiry.
branches.cn: 仪器服务于严谨探究。

intro.en: Scientific joins the science family of knowledge words.
intro.cn: scientific 加入由知识词汇构成的 science 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scientificus is the direct model.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scientificus 是直接构词模型。

items.meaning: the group of scientists as a whole
items.example: The scientific community welcomed the result.

definition_en: a person who studies or works in science
core_image: 一位研究者俯身显微镜前，把刚看到的细节写进记录本
scene: 一位科学家在显微镜前记录观察结果。A scientist recorded her observations at the microscope.
sceneCN: 这里 scientist 是「科学家」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一位科学家在显微镜前记录观察结果。

senses.title: An expert in science
senses.definition: a person with expert knowledge of a science
senses.definitionCN: 拥有某门科学专业知识的人
senses.example: The scientist studied the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这位科学家研究了土壤。
senses.why: The core sense is a trained expert in a science.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是受过训练的科学专家。

senses.title: A researcher
senses.definition: a person who does scientific research
senses.definitionCN: 从事科学研究的人员
senses.example: Scientists warn about the risk.
senses.exampleCN: 科研人员警告这种风险。
senses.why: The role also covers people whose main work is research.
senses.whyCN: 这一称谓也涵盖以研究为主要工作的人。

intro.en: Scientist is science plus ist, a word coined in the 19th century.
intro.cn: scientist 由 science 加 ist 构成，是 19 世纪新造的词。

items.en: Scientia meant knowledge.
items.cn: scientia 意为知识。

items.en: Science narrowed to mean the study of nature.
items.cn: science 缩小为对自然的研究。

items.en: The word scientist was coined for people who study nature.
items.cn: scientist 一词被创造出来，指研究自然的人。

items.en: Scientist spread to every field of research.
items.cn: scientist 扩展到各个研究领域。

items.en: Scientist now means any trained researcher in science.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scientist 指任何受过训练的科研人员。

note.en: Scientist is compared with related words and with names for researchers.
note.cn: 把 scientist 与相关词以及表示研究者的名称作比较。

entries.definition: a person who studies a subject carefully

normalIntro.en: Scientist is science plus ist, the person who does the science.
normalIntro.cn: scientist 是 science 加 ist，即从事科学的人。

normal.en: Science is the field and scientist is the person.
normal.cn: science 是领域，scientist 是人。

normal.en: A computer scientist works with computing.
normal.cn: 计算机科学家研究计算。

normal.en: A social scientist studies people.
normal.cn: 社会科学家研究人。

normal.en: The ist ending often marks a person.
normal.cn: ist 结尾常表示人。

normal.en: Scientists test ideas before accepting them.
normal.cn: 科学家在接受想法前先检验它。

abstract.en: The word was invented when science became a profession.
abstract.cn: 当科学成为职业时，这个词被创造出来。

abstract.en: A scientist is defined by method, not by a single subject.
abstract.cn: 科学家的定义在于方法，而不限于单一学科。

abstract.en: The ist suffix turns a body of knowledge into a role.
abstract.cn: ist 后缀把知识体系变成一种角色。

examples.en: She became a scientist at twenty-five.
examples.cn: 她二十五岁时成为科学家。

examples.en: The scientists published their findings.
examples.cn: 科学家们发表了研究结果。

examples.en: A young scientist led the project.
examples.cn: 一位年轻科学家领导了这个项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: science 是「科学」，ist 表示「从事……的人」，scientist 就是从事科学研究的人。

root: 由 science（科学）加表人后缀 ist 构成，19 世纪开始广泛使用。

sensesIntro.en: Scientist means an expert in a science or a person who does scientific research.
sensesIntro.cn: scientist 意为某门科学的专家，或从事科学研究的人。

core.en: A person whose work is producing scientific knowledge.
core.cn: 以产出科学知识为工作的人。

branches.en: A trained expert in one science.
branches.cn: 某门科学中受过训练的专家。

branches.en: A person whose daily work is research.
branches.cn: 以研究为日常工作的人。

branches.en: Expertise and research usually go together.
branches.cn: 专业知识与研究通常相伴。

branches.en: Both senses describe a scientific worker.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述科学工作者。

branches.en: The role can be in a lab, a field, or a classroom.
branches.cn: 这一角色可以出现在实验室、田野或课堂。

intro.en: Scientist belongs to the science family of people and methods.
intro.cn: scientist 属于由人物与方法词汇构成的 science 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scientia, knowledge, is the distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scientia（知识）是远源。

items.exampleCN: 科学家提出了一个问题。
社会科学家研究了人群。

items.example: The computer scientist fixed the code.
items.exampleCN: 计算机科学家修复了代码。

definition_en: a cutting tool with two blades joined in the middle, or a scissor-like movement in sport
core_image: 桌上摊着彩纸，一把银色剪刀停在剪了一半的星星边
scene: 她拿起剪刀，把彩纸剪成星星。She picked up the scissors and cut the paper into stars.
sceneCN: 这里 scissors 是「剪刀」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她拿起剪刀，把彩纸剪成星星。

senses.title: A cutting tool
senses.definition: a tool with two blades joined in the middle that cuts when closed
senses.definitionCN: 中间相连、合拢时切割的两片刀刃工具
senses.example: These scissors are sharp.
senses.why: The core sense is the everyday cutting tool.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是日常切割工具。

senses.title: A scissor movement
senses.definition: a movement or hold in which two parts cross like blades
senses.definitionCN: 两部分像刀刃一样交叉的动作或夹持
senses.example: He won the match with a scissors hold.
senses.exampleCN: 他用剪式夹持赢得了比赛。
senses.why: The tool's crossing shape names a movement in sport.
senses.whyCN: 工具交叉的形状被用来命名体育动作。

intro.en: Scissors comes from Latin cisoria, cutting tools, from caedere, to cut.
intro.cn: scissors 源自拉丁语 cisoria（切割工具），来自 caedere（切）。

items.en: Caedere meant to cut or strike.
items.cn: caedere 意为切或砍。

items.en: Cisoria meant cutting tools.
items.cn: cisoria 意为切割工具。

items.en: Cisoires named a pair of cutting blades.
items.cn: cisoires 指成对的切割刀片。

items.en: Sisoures entered English as a plural word.
items.cn: sisoures 以复数形式进入英语。

items.en: Scissors keeps its plural form for one tool.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scissors 指一件工具却保留复数形式。

note.en: Scissors is compared with similar-looking words and with other cutting tools.
note.cn: 把 scissors 与形近词以及其他切割工具作比较。

entries.definition: large scissors for cutting plants or metal
tools for cutting hair or nails
a tool or person that cuts

normalIntro.en: Scissors looks plural because it names two joined blades.
normalIntro.cn: scissors 看似复数，因为它指两片相连的刀刃。

normal.en: A pair of scissors is one tool.
normal.cn: a pair of scissors 指一件工具。

normal.en: Nail scissors are small and curved.
normal.cn: 指甲剪小而弯曲。

normal.en: Cut paper with scissors.
normal.cn: 用剪刀剪纸。

normal.en: Scissor is also a verb meaning to cut.
normal.cn: scissor 也可作动词，意为剪。

normal.en: Running with scissors is dangerous.
normal.cn: 拿着剪刀跑很危险。

abstract.en: Two blades cross, and the crossing gives the word its shape.
abstract.cn: 两片刀刃交叉，交叉的形状赋予这个词形象。

abstract.en: The plural form survives because the tool is made of two parts.
abstract.cn: 复数形式保留下来，因为这件工具由两部分组成。

abstract.en: The cutting action becomes a name for scissor movements.
abstract.cn: 切割动作又成为剪式动作的名称。

examples.en: Cut the thread with scissors.
The child dropped the scissors.
She keeps scissors in the drawer.

dict_mnemonic.text: scissors 来自拉丁语 caedere（切），原指切割工具；英语里常用复数形式 a pair of scissors。

root: 源自拉丁语 cisoria（切割工具），来自 caedere（切），核心义「成对刀片构成的切割工具」。

sensesIntro.en: Scissors means a cutting tool with two joined blades, or a crossing movement in sport.
sensesIntro.cn: scissors 意为两片刀刃相连的切割工具，或体育中的交叉剪式动作。

core.en: Two blades that cut by crossing.
core.cn: 通过交叉来切割的两片刀刃。

branches.en: A hand tool for cutting paper or cloth.

branches.cn: 切割与交叉构成同一个核心概念。

intro.en: Scissors forms compounds for tools and sports movements.
intro.cn: scissors 构成表示工具与体育动作的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cisoria and caedere are the sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cisoria 与 caedere 是词源。

items.example: She scored with a scissor kick.
The wrestler used a scissor hold.
Nail scissors are in the bathroom.

items.example: I need a pair of scissors.

senses.title: Points in a game

senses.whyCN: 核心现代义是竞赛中的得分。

senses.title: A mark or result
senses.definition: the result of a test or assessment
senses.definitionCN: 考试或评估的结果

senses.whyCN: 比赛义延伸到任何被测量的结果。

senses.title: A group of twenty

senses.title: Music for a film
senses.definition: the music written for a film, play, or show
senses.definitionCN: 为电影、戏剧或演出创作的音乐
senses.example: The film score was written in a month.

intro.en: Score comes from Old Norse skor, a notch or tally mark.

items.en: Skor meant a notch cut into wood.
items.cn: skor 意为刻在木头上的刻痕。

items.en: Score named a tally kept by notches.
items.cn: score 指用刻痕记录的账目。

items.en: A score of twenty became a standard count.
items.cn: 以二十为一组的计数成为标准。

items.en: Score named the points kept in games.
items.cn: score 开始指比赛中记录的分数。

items.en: Score also means written music for a film or play.
items.cn: 现代英语中 score 还指电影或戏剧的配乐。

note.en: Score is compared with similar-looking words and with words for points and marks.
note.cn: 把 score 与形近词以及表示分数与成绩的词作比较。

entries.definition: a unit of score in a game

normalIntro.en: Score began as a notch used for counting and now names points and music.
normalIntro.cn: score 起初是计数用的刻痕，现在指得分与配乐。

normal.en: The final score decides the winner.
normal.cn: 最终比分决定胜者。

normal.en: A test score measures a result.
normal.cn: 考试分数衡量结果。

normal.en: A score of people means twenty people.
normal.cn: a score of people 指二十个人。

normal.en: A film score is its music.
normal.cn: film score 是电影配乐。

normal.en: To score is to win a point.
normal.cn: to score 就是得分。

abstract.en: Counting by notches connects twenty, games, and music.
abstract.cn: 刻痕计数把二十、比赛与音乐连接起来。

abstract.en: A score is a record of what has been counted.
abstract.cn: score 是被计数内容的记录。

abstract.en: Music on a page is also a kind of tally of sounds.
abstract.cn: 纸上的音乐也是一种声音的记录。

examples.en: The final score was three to two.
Her test score improved.
The film score won an award.
examples.cn: 这部电影的配乐获了奖。

dict_mnemonic.text: score 源自古诺尔斯语 skor（刻痕），古人用刻痕计数，二十为一组，所以 score 又有「二十」义；比赛记分也来自刻痕计数。

root: 源自古诺尔斯语 skor（刻痕、计数刻线），核心义「用刻痕记录的数量与得分」。

sensesIntro.en: Score means points in a game, a test result, a group of twenty, or music for a film.
sensesIntro.cn: score 意为比赛得分、考试成绩、二十，或电影配乐。

core.en: A record of counting, from notches to points.
core.cn: 从刻痕到得分的计数记录。

branches.en: Points recorded in a contest.
branches.cn: 比赛中记录的分数。

branches.en: A measured result on a test.
branches.cn: 考试中测量的结果。

branches.en: A counted group of twenty.
branches.cn: 计为一组的二十个。

branches.en: Written music for a production.
branches.cn: 为演出写下的音乐。

branches.en: Games and tests both turn performance into numbers.
branches.cn: 比赛与考试都把表现转化为数字。

intro.en: Score forms words for scoring, players, and music marks.
intro.cn: score 构成表示记分、得分者与音乐记号的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Old Norse skor is the source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古诺尔斯语 skor 是词源，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: Scores rose after the new rules.
items.exampleCN: 新规则实施后分数上升。

items.example: Scoring is easy in this game.

items.meaning: to emphasize or draw a line under

items.exampleCN: 这部电影配乐萦绕人心。

definition_zh: 屏幕；银幕；屏风；筛查；遮挡
definition_en: a flat surface showing images, the cinema, a protective panel, to examine for suitability, or to hide something
core_image: 黑暗的客厅里，电视屏幕忽然亮起，映出一张脸
scene: 手机屏幕在黑暗的房间里亮了起来。The phone screen lit up in the dark room.
sceneCN: 这里 screen 是「屏幕」（第 1 个义项）；句意：手机屏幕在黑暗的房间里亮了起来。

senses.title: A display surface
senses.definition: a flat surface on which images or words are shown
senses.definitionCN: 显示图像或文字的平面
senses.example: The phone screen lit up in the dark room.
senses.exampleCN: 手机屏幕在黑暗的房间里亮了起来。
senses.why: The central modern sense is the surface that shows images.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义是显示图像的表面。

senses.title: The cinema
senses.definition: the large screen in a cinema, or film as a medium
senses.definitionCN: 电影院的大银幕，或作为媒介的电影
senses.example: The film was shown on a big screen.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影在大银幕上放映。
senses.why: The display surface stands for the medium shown on it.
senses.whyCN: 显示表面代指在其上呈现的媒介。

senses.title: A protective panel
senses.definition: a piece of material used to block view, wind, or light
senses.definitionCN: 用于挡视线、挡风或遮光的材料
senses.example: A folding screen divided the room.
senses.why: The oldest sense is something that stands in front.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是挡在前面的东西。

senses.title: To examine for suitability
senses.definition: to check people or things to decide if they are suitable or safe
senses.definitionCN: 检查人或物以判断是否合适或安全
senses.example: Doctors screen patients for the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 医生为病人筛查这种疾病。
senses.why: A screen separates what passes from what does not.
senses.whyCN: 筛子把通过者与不通过者分开。

senses.title: To hide from view
senses.definition: to protect or hide something behind a screen
senses.definitionCN: 把某物挡在遮蔽物后面以保护或隐藏
senses.example: Clouds screened the sun.
senses.why: The panel sense becomes the act of blocking.
senses.whyCN: 遮蔽物义转变为遮挡动作。

intro.en: Screen comes from Old French escren, a screen or shield, probably from Middle Dutch scherm.
intro.cn: screen 源自古法语 escren（屏风、遮挡物），可能来自中古荷兰语 scherm。

items.en: Scherm meant a shield or protection.
items.cn: scherm 意为盾牌或保护物。

items.en: Escren meant a screen against heat or view.
items.cn: escren 意为挡热或挡视线的屏风。

items.en: Screen named a panel that blocks view or wind.
items.cn: screen 指遮挡视线或风的屏风。

items.en: Screen came to mean a surface for showing images.
items.cn: screen 开始指显示图像的表面。

items.en: Screen also means to examine or to hide.
items.cn: 现代英语中 screen 还表示筛查或遮挡。

note.en: Screen is compared with similar-looking words and with words for displays and filters.
note.cn: 把 screen 与形近词以及表示显示和筛选的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flow of water or data
a screen used with a computer

normalIntro.en: Screen began as a shield and now names displays and filtering.
normalIntro.cn: screen 起初是遮挡物，现在指显示屏与筛选。

normal.en: A screen shows images.
normal.cn: 屏幕显示图像。

normal.en: The big screen means the cinema.
normal.cn: the big screen 指电影院。

normal.en: A screen can block wind or light.
normal.cn: 屏风可以挡风或遮光。

normal.en: To screen patients is to test them.
normal.cn: 筛查病人就是检测他们。

normal.en: Sunscreen screens the skin from the sun.
normal.cn: 防晒霜为皮肤遮挡阳光。

abstract.en: A screen both shows and hides.
abstract.cn: 屏幕既展示，也遮蔽。

abstract.en: The idea of a barrier links panels, displays, and filters.
abstract.cn: 屏障概念连接了屏风、显示屏与筛子。

abstract.en: To screen is to decide what may pass.
abstract.cn: 筛查就是决定什么可以通过。

examples.en: The film was shown on a big screen.
examples.cn: 这部电影在大银幕上放映。

examples.en: Doctors screen patients for the disease.
examples.cn: 医生为病人筛查这种疾病。

examples.en: Clouds screened the sun.

dict_mnemonic.text: screen 原指挡风的屏风，后来指隔开视线的平面，再指电视与手机屏幕；「筛查」义来自「用筛子隔开」。

root: 源自古法语 escren（屏风、遮挡物），来自中古荷兰语 scherm，核心义「挡在面前的一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Screen means a display surface, the cinema, a protective panel, to examine, or to hide something.
sensesIntro.cn: screen 意为显示屏、电影、屏风、筛查，或遮挡。

core.en: A surface that shows, hides, or separates.
core.cn: 用于显示、遮蔽或分隔的表面。

branches.en: A surface that shows images.
branches.cn: 显示图像的表面。

branches.en: The cinema as a medium.
branches.cn: 作为媒介的电影。

branches.en: A panel that blocks view or wind.
branches.cn: 遮挡视线或风的屏风。

branches.en: Testing and hiding both separate something.
branches.cn: 筛查与遮挡都在分离某物。

branches.en: A screen can reveal and conceal at once.
branches.cn: 屏幕可以同时呈现与遮蔽。

intro.en: Screen forms words for films, devices, and protection.
intro.cn: screen 构成表示电影、设备与保护的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Old French escren is the source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 escren 是词源，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The windows were screened from view.

items.meaning: a test or a film showing
an image shown on an idle screen

items.example: The story returned to the big screen.

definition_en: the large body of salt water covering much of the earth, a large amount, or the state of the waves
core_image: 蓝色海面一直延伸到天际，白色浪花一层层涌上沙滩
scene: 孩子们光着脚跑向海边。The children ran barefoot toward the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 sea 是「海；海洋」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们光着脚跑向海边。

senses.title: The salt water body
senses.definition: the large body of salt water that covers much of the earth
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体
senses.example: The sea was calm at dawn.
senses.why: The central sense is the great body of salt water.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是巨大的咸水体。

senses.title: A huge amount
senses.definition: a very large number or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物数量极多的一大片
senses.example: A sea of people filled the square.
senses.why: A boundless expanse becomes an image of great quantity.
senses.whyCN: 无边无际的景象成为数量的比喻。

senses.title: The state of the waves
senses.definition: the condition of the waves on the sea
senses.definitionCN: 海面上波浪的状况
senses.example: The ship sailed into rough seas.
senses.exampleCN: 船驶入了波涛汹涌的海面。
senses.why: The place sense narrows to the water's surface condition.
senses.whyCN: 场所义缩小为水面状况。

intro.en: Sea comes from Old English sæ, a word shared with other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: sea 源自古英语 sæ，与其他日耳曼语言同源。

items.en: Sæ meant the sea or a large lake.
items.cn: sæ 意为海或大湖。

items.en: See named the great body of salt water.
items.cn: see 指巨大的咸水体。

items.en: Sea appeared in many compounds for travel and trade.
items.cn: sea 大量出现在航海与贸易复合词中。

items.en: A sea of something became a common image of quantity.
items.cn: a sea of 成为表示数量的常见比喻。

items.en: Sea means the ocean, its surface, or a vast amount.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sea 指海洋、海面或大量。

note.en: Sea is compared with similar short words and with words for large waters.
note.cn: 把 sea 与形近短词以及表示大片水域的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sea animal, or a stamp
one of the great bodies of salt water
the clear liquid in seas and rivers

normalIntro.en: Sea is the salt water, its waves, and any vast expanse.
normalIntro.cn: sea 是咸水、海浪，也是任何广阔的景象。

normal.en: Sea and see sound the same.
normal.cn: sea 与 see 发音相同。

normal.en: By the sea means near the coast.
normal.cn: by the sea 意为在海边。

normal.en: Sea level is the height of the ocean surface.
normal.cn: sea level 是海平面高度。

normal.en: Seafood comes from the sea.
normal.cn: 海鲜来自海洋。

normal.en: A sea of faces means a huge crowd.
normal.cn: a sea of faces 指人山人海。

abstract.en: A boundless surface easily becomes a metaphor for quantity.
abstract.cn: 无边无际的表面很容易成为数量的比喻。

abstract.en: The same word names the water, its waves, and its scale.
abstract.cn: 同一个词命名水体、波浪与规模。

abstract.en: Sea connects geography with feeling.
abstract.cn: sea 把地理与情感连接起来。

examples.en: The sea was calm at dawn.
They live by the sea.
A sea of people filled the square.

dict_mnemonic.text: sea 是「海」，与 see 同音；seaside 是海滨，seafood 是海鲜，sea level 是海平面。

root: 源自古英语 sæ（海、大湖），核心义「覆盖大片地表的咸水体」。

sensesIntro.en: Sea means the salt water body, a vast amount, or the condition of the waves.
sensesIntro.cn: sea 意为海洋、大量，或海面波浪状况。

core.en: A vast body of salt water.
core.cn: 巨大的咸水体。

branches.en: The ocean itself.
branches.cn: 海洋本身。

branches.en: A crowd or amount like an ocean.
branches.cn: 像海洋一样的数量或人群。

branches.en: The movement and mood of the water.
branches.cn: 水面的运动与状态。

branches.en: The vast body inspires images of scale.
branches.cn: 巨大的水体激发规模想象。

branches.en: Water and waves are one experience.
branches.cn: 海水与波浪是同一体验。

intro.en: Sea forms compounds for coast, travel, and food.
intro.cn: sea 构成表示海岸、航海与食物的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Old English sæ is the source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 sæ 是词源，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: We spent a week at the seaside.

items.exampleCN: 这个海港承担大量贸易。

items.meaning: a bird that lives near the sea
the average height of the sea
items.example: The town lies below sea level.

definition_en: a sea animal with flippers, a stamped mark, a closed fastening, or to close something tightly
core_image: 一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳，胡须上还挂着水珠
scene: 一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳。A seal lay on the ice in the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 seal 是「海豹」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳。

senses.title: A sea animal
senses.definition: a sea animal with flippers that rests on land or ice
senses.definitionCN: 有鳍状肢、在陆地或冰上休息的海洋动物
senses.example: A seal swam beside the boat.
senses.why: One word comes from an old name for this animal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的一个来源就是这种动物的古称。

senses.title: A stamped mark
senses.definition: a device or mark pressed onto a document to prove it is genuine
senses.definitionCN: 盖在文件上以证明其真实的器具或印记
senses.example: The letter bore the king's seal.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信上有国王的印章。
senses.why: A pressed mark closes and certifies a document.
senses.whyCN: 压印的标记封闭并证明文件。

senses.title: A closed fastening
senses.definition: something that closes an opening tightly
senses.definitionCN: 把开口紧密封闭的东西
senses.example: The seal on the jar was broken.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子上的封口被打开了。
senses.why: The certified mark becomes a physical closure.
senses.whyCN: 认证标记变成物理封口。

senses.title: To close tightly
senses.definition: to close something so that air or liquid cannot pass
senses.definitionCN: 封闭某物使空气或液体无法通过
senses.example: She sealed the envelope with wax.
senses.why: The noun of closure becomes the action of closing.
senses.whyCN: 封闭物的名词义转为封闭动作。

intro.en: Seal is two words in one: Old English seolh, the animal, and Latin sigillum, a small stamp.
intro.cn: seal 是两个词合流：古英语 seolh（海豹）与拉丁语 sigillum（小图章）。

items.en: Seolh named the sea animal.
items.cn: seolh 指海豹这种海洋动物。

items.en: Sigillum meant a small picture or stamp.
items.cn: sigillum 意为小图像或印章。

items.en: Seel meant a stamp used on documents.
items.cn: seel 指用于文件的印章。

items.en: Seal named both the animal and the stamp.
items.cn: seal 同时指海豹与印章。

items.en: Seal also meant to close a document formally.
items.cn: seal 也开始表示正式封住文件。

items.en: Seal means to close tightly or to block an area.
items.cn: 现代英语中 seal 意为密封或封锁区域。

note.en: Seal is compared with similar short words and with words for stamps and closures.
note.cn: 把 seal 与形近短词以及表示印章和封闭的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small mark or device pressed on paper
a small seal, often in a ring

normalIntro.en: Seal is an animal and also a stamp that closes a document.
normalIntro.cn: seal 既是海豹，也是封住文件的印章。

normal.en: A seal lives in cold seas.
normal.cn: 海豹生活在寒冷海域。

normal.en: A wax seal closes a letter.
normal.cn: 蜡封印封住信件。

normal.en: Seal the envelope before posting.
normal.cn: 寄出前把信封封好。

normal.en: Police sealed off the street.
normal.cn: 警察封锁了街道。

normal.en: Seal and sea look alike.
normal.cn: seal 与 sea 形近。

abstract.en: Two unrelated words became one spelling.
abstract.cn: 两个无关的词变成了同一个拼写。

abstract.en: A stamp that proves a document also closes it.
abstract.cn: 证明文件的印章同时也封闭文件。

abstract.en: Closing and certifying share one gesture.
abstract.cn: 封闭与认证共享同一个动作。

examples.en: The envelope was sealed with wax.
Police sealed off the street.
A seal swam beside the boat.

dict_mnemonic.text: seal 有两个来源：古英语 seolh 指海豹，拉丁语 sigillum 指印章；「密封」义从盖印章封住文件发展而来。

root: 双源词：海豹义来自古英语 seolh；印章与密封义来自拉丁语 sigillum（小图章）。

sensesIntro.en: Seal means a sea animal, a stamped mark, a closure, or to close something tightly.
sensesIntro.cn: seal 意为海豹、印章、封口，或密封。

core.en: A mark or closure that makes something secure.
core.cn: 使某物安全可靠的印记或封闭。

branches.en: The animal of cold seas.
branches.cn: 寒冷海域的动物。

branches.en: A mark that proves a document.
branches.cn: 证明文件的印记。

branches.en: A physical closure on a container.
branches.cn: 容器上的物理封口。

branches.en: The action of closing tightly.
branches.cn: 紧密封闭的动作。

branches.en: Stamping and sealing both finish a document.
branches.cn: 盖章与密封都完成文件处理。

intro.en: Seal forms words for closing materials and actions.
intro.cn: seal 构成表示密封材料与动作的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin sigillum is the source of the stamp sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sigillum 是印章义的来源。

items.meaning: an animal, a stamp, or to close

items.example: Sealing the jar keeps food fresh.
items.exampleCN: 密封罐子能让食物保鲜。

items.meaning: a substance or person that seals

items.exampleCN: 法院公开了密封的记录。

items.example: He wore a silver seal ring.
items.exampleCN: 他戴着一枚银印章戒指。

definition_en: to look carefully for something, to examine a place, or the act of looking
core_image: 手电筒的光柱在黑暗房间里来回移动，寻找丢失的钥匙
scene: 他们在黑暗的房间里寻找钥匙。They searched the dark room for the key.
sceneCN: 这里 search 是「搜索；寻找」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们在黑暗的房间里寻找钥匙。

senses.title: To look for something
senses.definition: to look carefully for something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 仔细寻找某物或某人
senses.example: She searched for her keys.
senses.why: The central sense is looking for something lost or wanted.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是寻找丢失或想要的东西。

senses.title: To examine a place
senses.definition: to examine a place or person thoroughly
senses.definitionCN: 彻底检查某个地方或某个人
senses.example: The police searched the house.
senses.why: Looking for something becomes a formal examination of a place.
senses.whyCN: 寻找某物变成对场所的正式检查。

senses.title: An act of looking
senses.definition: an attempt to find something
senses.definitionCN: 寻找某物的尝试
senses.example: The search took two hours.
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun for the whole effort.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为表示整个努力过程的名词。

intro.en: Search comes from Old French cerchier, from Latin circare, to go around.
intro.cn: search 源自古法语 cerchier，来自拉丁语 circare（绕行）。

items.en: Circare meant to go around or wander over.
items.cn: circare 意为绕行或走遍。

items.en: Cerchier meant to look through a place.
items.cn: cerchier 意为搜遍一个地方。

items.en: Serchen meant to examine or look for.
items.cn: serchen 意为检查或寻找。

items.en: Search named an official examination.
items.cn: search 指正式检查。

items.en: Search covers looking, examining, and online finding.
items.cn: 现代英语中 search 涵盖寻找、搜查与网络检索。

note.en: Search is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs for seeking.
note.cn: 把 search 与形近词以及表示寻找的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a place where a bird rests

senses.title: To introduce the second point in a list
senses.definition: used to introduce the second item, reason, or argument after «first» or «firstly»
senses.definitionCN: 在 first 或 firstly 之后，用来引出第二项、第二条理由或第二个论点
senses.example: First, the plan is cheap. Secondly, it is easy to carry out.
senses.exampleCN: 第一，这个方案很省钱。其次，它很容易实施。
senses.why: The ordinal number second names what comes after the first, and the adverb ending -ly turns it into a signpost word that guides listeners through a list.
senses.whyCN: 序数词 second 表示「排在第一之后的那个」，加上副词后缀 -ly 后变成路标词，专门在列举时为听众指引第二个要点。

senses.title: To add a second, supporting argument
senses.titleCN: 追加第二条支持性论据
senses.definition: used in formal writing or debate to add a further reason that strengthens the case already made
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式写作或辩论中，补充一条强化前文立场的进一步理由
senses.example: The rule is unfair; secondly, it would be almost impossible to enforce.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规定不公平；其次，它几乎无法执行。
senses.why: Once a list frame is established, the speaker naturally reuses the same signpost pattern to stack reasons, so secondly grows from naming a position into carrying a new supporting argument.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「列条目」的框架建立起来，说话者就自然复用同一路标模式来叠加理由，secondly 便从「标记位置」长出「承载新论据」的功能。

intro.en: Secondly is a modern signpost adverb built from the ordinal number second plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: secondly 是现代英语里的列举路标副词，由序数词 second 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: The root is Latin secundus, meaning «following, next in order», from the verb sequi, «to follow».
items.cn: 词根是拉丁语 secundus，意为「跟随其后的、依次的下一个」，来自动词 sequi「跟随」。

items.en: Latin secundus passed into Old French as second, keeping the meaning of «next after the first».
items.cn: 拉丁语 secundus 进入古法语变成 second，仍表示「紧跟第一之后的」。

items.en: Middle English borrowed second from Old French around the thirteenth century as an ordinal adjective.
items.cn: 中古英语约在十三世纪从古法语借入 second，作序数形容词使用。

items.en: In Modern English, second combined with the productive adverb suffix -ly to form secondly, first recorded as a discourse marker in formal argument.
items.cn: 现代英语中，second 与能产性副词后缀 -ly 结合形成 secondly，最早记录为正式论证中的话语标记。

items.en: Today secondly normally appears only in enumerated speech or writing, paired with firstly or first, and is not used for the physical sense of «the second time».
items.cn: 如今 secondly 一般只出现在列条目的口语或书面语中，与 firstly 或 first 配对使用，不用于表示「第二次」这类实际次数含义。

note.en: Secondly is easy to confuse with its cousin words built on the same ordinal root.
note.cn: secondly 容易与同根的序数词族词混淆，下面两组帮你分清。

entries.definition: in addition; used to add another stronger point

entries.definition: coming immediately after in order or sequence

normalIntro.en: Five grounded ways to remember secondly.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于构词和搭配的记忆法。

normal.en: second + -ly: the ordinal number second «next after first» plus the common adverb suffix -ly, exactly like «firstly».
normal.cn: second（第二）加副词后缀 -ly，构造与 firstly（第一）完全平行。

normal.en: Latin sequi «to follow»: secondly marks the point that follows the first one.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 sequi「跟随」：secondly 标记的就是「跟在第一点后面」的那一点。

normal.en: Pair memory: whenever you hear firstly, expect secondly to arrive next.
normal.cn: 配对记忆：听到 firstly，下一个多半就是 secondly。

normal.en: Speech skeleton: firstly… secondly… finally… is the classic three-point speech frame.
normal.cn: 演讲骨架：firstly… secondly… finally… 是经典的三点式发言框架。

normal.en: Essay signpost: in argumentative writing, secondly opens the second body paragraph.
normal.cn: 写作路标：议论文里 secondly 常开启第二个主体段落。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder: you have stepped on rung one (firstly) and now lift your foot to rung two — secondly.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子：已踩上第一级（firstly），正抬脚踏上第二级——secondly。

abstract.en: Two checkboxes on a to-do list: the first is ticked, your pen hovers over the second — that hover is secondly.
abstract.cn: 待办清单上两个方框：第一个已打勾，笔尖悬在第二个上方——这一悬停就是 secondly。

abstract.en: A train leaving station one and pulling into station two: each stop of the argument is a numbered platform.
abstract.cn: 列车驶离一站、进站二：论证的每一站都是编了号的月台，secondly 就是第二月台到站声。

examples.en: Firstly, the room is too small; secondly, the rent is too high.
examples.cn: 第一，房间太小；其次，租金太高。

examples.en: Secondly, we must think about how the new rule affects younger students.
examples.cn: 其次，我们必须考虑新规定对低年级学生的影响。

examples.en: She listed two reasons: secondly, the bus would be faster than walking.
examples.cn: 她列了两条理由：其次，坐公交比走路快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞看得了」——第一点已经看完了，塞进脑子里看第二点，看得了第二点就轮到 secondly。

root: 拉丁语 secundus（依次的、跟随其后的）← 动词 sequi（跟随）；经古法语 second 进入中古英语；现代英语加副词后缀 -ly 构成列举路标词。

sensesIntro.en: Two discourse senses: a list signpost, and a carrier for the second supporting argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个话语义项：既是列举路标，也是第二条支持性论据的载体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stepping to the second mark on an ordered list

branches.en: ENUMERATION: secondly names the second point after first or firstly.
branches.cn: 列举线：secondly 在 first 或 firstly 之后点名第二个要点。

branches.en: ARGUMENT: the second point is stacked to reinforce the case already opened.
branches.cn: 论证线：第二个要点用来强化已经展开的立场。

branches.en: SEQUENCE: it inherits the Latin idea of following what came before.
branches.cn: 顺序线：它继承了拉丁语「跟随在前者之后」的观念。

branches.en: SIGNPOST: the -ly form works like firstly and finally to structure speech.
branches.cn: 路标线：-ly 形式与 firstly、finally 一样为发言搭建结构。

branches.en: FORMALITY: it marks formal, planned discourse rather than casual chat.
branches.cn: 语域线：它标记正式、有准备的语篇，而非随意闲谈。

intro.en: Secondly is a transparent formation: ordinal stem + adverb suffix.
intro.cn: secondly 构词透明：序数词干加副词后缀，一目了然。

latinIntro.en: The ordinal stem traces back to Latin secundus «following».
latinIntro.cn: 序数词干可追溯到拉丁语 secundus「跟随其后的」。

normal.cn: 生病时你去看医生。

normal.en: A city can see many changes over time.
normal.cn: 一座城市会经历许多变化。

normal.en: See, look, and watch differ in how long you attend.
normal.cn: see、look、watch 在注视时长上不同。

abstract.en: To see is to let the world enter you.
abstract.cn: 看见，就是让世界进入你。

abstract.en: Understanding is sight turned inward.
abstract.cn: 理解是转向内心的视力。

abstract.en: What we have seen shapes what we expect to see.
abstract.cn: 我们见过的东西，塑造了我们期待看见的东西。

examples.en: I saw a light in the window.
I see what you mean.
The city has seen many changes.
examples.cn: 这座城市经历了许多变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: see 是日耳曼语本族词，靠高频使用记忆：see、saw、seen 三态，另有名词 sight。

root: 源自古英语 seon（看见），属日耳曼语本族词，核心义「用眼睛感知」。

sensesIntro.en: See means to perceive with the eyes, to understand, to meet, or to experience.
sensesIntro.cn: see 意为看见、明白、会见或经历。

core.en: To take something in through the eyes, and then through the mind.
core.cn: 先用眼睛、再用心智去接收某物。

branches.en: Light reaches the eyes.
branches.cn: 光线进入眼睛。

branches.en: A point becomes clear in the mind.
branches.cn: 某个要点在心中变得清楚。

branches.en: One person comes before another.
branches.cn: 一个人出现在另一个人面前。

branches.en: An event is lived through.
branches.cn: 一个事件被亲历。

branches.en: Seeing and understanding share one verb.
branches.cn: 看见与明白共用一个动词。

intro.en: See is a native Germanic verb with several compounds built on sight.
intro.cn: see 是日耳曼语本族动词，并由 sight 构成若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: This is a Germanic word, so there are no Latin base forms to add.
latinIntro.cn: 这是日耳曼语词，没有对应的拉丁语词根条目。

items.example: Can you see the tower from here?
items.exampleCN: 你从这里能看见那座塔吗？
这本书提供了真正的洞察。

items.example: No one could foresee the result.

items.meaning: a person who claims to see the future
items.example: The old seer warned of a storm.
items.exampleCN: 那位老先知警告将有风暴。

definition_en: to appear to be something or to appear to do something, or to make a statement less direct
core_image: 雾里一个模糊的人影，轮廓忽近忽远
scene: 雾里那个人影晃了一下，看着像熟人。The figure seemed familiar in the fog.
sceneCN: 这里 seem 是「看起来像」（第 1 个义项）；句意：雾中的身影看起来很熟悉。

senses.title: Appear to be
senses.definition: to give the impression of being something
senses.definitionCN: 给人某种印象，好像是某物
senses.example: The house seems very old.
senses.why: This is the common linking use before an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这是接形容词时最常见的系动词用法。

senses.title: Appear to do
senses.definition: to give the impression of doing something
senses.definitionCN: 给人正在做某事的印象
senses.example: She seems to know the answer.
senses.why: Seem can also introduce an action.
senses.whyCN: seem 也可以引出某个动作。

senses.title: Softening a statement
senses.definition: used to make a claim less direct or less certain
senses.definitionCN: 用于让陈述更委婉、更不确定
senses.example: It seems we have a problem.
senses.why: The word softens what follows it.
senses.whyCN: 该词使其后的说法变得委婉。

intro.en: Seem comes from Old Norse soema, to befit, from a root meaning fitting or suitable.
intro.cn: seem 源自古诺斯语 soema（适合），词根意为「相称、合适」。

items.en: Soema meant to befit or suit.
items.cn: soema 意为适合、相称。

items.en: The related adjective meant fitting.
items.cn: 相关形容词意为合适的。

items.en: English seem first meant to be fitting.
items.cn: 英语 seem 最初意为合适。

items.en: It shifted toward appear to be.
items.cn: 它逐渐转向「看起来是」的意思。

items.en: It now also softens statements politely.
items.cn: 如今它也用来礼貌地缓和陈述。

note.en: Seem is compared with similar-looking words and with other linking verbs.
note.cn: 把 seem 与形近词以及其他系动词作比较。

entries.definition: the part of a plant that grows
to look as if something is true
to give a certain impression when heard

normalIntro.en: Seem means to look a certain way without proving it.
normalIntro.cn: seem 意为看起来如此，但并未证实。

normal.en: Seem is a linking verb like appear.
normal.cn: seem 和 appear 一样是系动词。

normal.en: It seems that means it appears that.
normal.cn: it seems that 意为「看起来……」。

normal.en: She seems tired means she looks tired.
normal.cn: she seems tired 意为她看起来很累。

normal.en: Seem to do describes an apparent action.
normal.cn: seem to do 描述一个看似发生的动作。

normal.en: Seemly and unseemly come from the same root.
normal.cn: seemly 与 unseemly 同出一源。

abstract.en: Seem lives in the gap between appearance and fact.
abstract.cn: seem 存在于外表与事实的缝隙里。

abstract.en: What seems true may only be partly true.
abstract.cn: 看似为真的，也许只是部分为真。

abstract.en: Every judgment begins with how things seem.
abstract.cn: 每个判断都始于事物呈现的样子。

examples.en: The house seems very old.
She seems to know the answer.
It seems we have a problem.

dict_mnemonic.text: seem 借自古诺斯语 soema（适合），由「相称」引申为「显得、似乎」，是常见的系动词。

root: 源自古诺斯语 soema（适合、相称），核心义「看上去相称、像是如此」。

sensesIntro.en: Seem means to appear to be, to appear to do, or to make a statement softer.
sensesIntro.cn: seem 意为似乎是、似乎做，或使陈述更委婉。

core.en: To present an appearance that may or may not be true.
core.cn: 呈现出可能真也可能不真的样子。

branches.en: Something gives a certain impression.
branches.cn: 某物给人某种印象。

branches.en: Someone looks as if doing something.
branches.cn: 某人看起来像是在做某事。

branches.en: A claim is made less direct.
branches.cn: 一个说法被说得更委婉。

branches.en: Both senses rest on appearance.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在外表之上。

branches.en: Politeness hides inside uncertainty.
branches.cn: 礼貌藏在不确定之中。

intro.en: Seem builds a small family around the idea of what is fitting.
intro.cn: seem 围绕「相称、得体」构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: This word came from Old Norse, so there are no Latin base forms to add.
latinIntro.cn: 该词来自古诺斯语，没有对应的拉丁语词根条目。

items.exampleCN: 她表面的平静掩盖着恐惧。

items.example: They argued in an unseemly way.
The unseemliness of the joke shocked her.
items.exampleCN: 这个笑话的粗俗让她震惊。

definition_en: to give something in exchange for money, to persuade people to buy something, or to be bought in a certain way
core_image: 集市刚开，摊主把一筐番茄摆到最前面
scene: 集市刚开，摊主就把番茄摆到最前面。They sell fresh vegetables every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 sell 是「出售」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们每天早上卖新鲜蔬菜。

senses.title: Give for money
senses.definition: to give something to someone in exchange for money
senses.definitionCN: 用某物换取金钱
senses.example: He sold his old bike.
senses.why: This is the basic commercial sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的交易义。

senses.title: Persuade to buy
senses.definition: to make something seem worth buying
senses.definitionCN: 使某物看起来值得购买
senses.example: The ad sells the idea of a simple life.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告推销的是一种简单生活的理念。
senses.why: Selling can also mean promoting an idea.
senses.whyCN: sell 也可以指推销一种理念。

senses.title: Be bought
senses.definition: to be bought in a particular way or amount
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式或数量被买走
senses.example: The book sold a million copies.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书卖出了上百万册。
senses.why: The intransitive use describes sales figures.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法描述销售情况。

intro.en: Sell comes from Old English sellan, to give or hand over, with the past form sold.
intro.cn: sell 源自古英语 sellan（给予、交出），过去式为 sold。

items.en: Sellan meant to give or hand over.
items.cn: sellan 意为给予或交出。

items.en: The past form sealde later became sold.
items.cn: 过去式 sealde 后来演变为 sold。

items.en: The verb narrowed toward selling goods.
items.cn: 该动词的意义收窄到出售货物。

items.en: Sell out named all goods being taken.
items.cn: sell out 指货物全部卖出。

items.en: Marketing extended sell to ideas and images.
items.cn: 营销把 sell 扩展到理念与形象。

note.en: Sell is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs of trade.
note.cn: 把 sell 与形近词以及表示交易的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to promote and sell a product

normalIntro.en: Sell means to exchange goods for money.
normalIntro.cn: sell 意为用货物换取金钱。

normal.en: The past tense of sell is sold.
normal.cn: sell 的过去式是 sold。

normal.en: A bestseller sells very well.
normal.cn: bestseller 是卖得极好的书。

normal.en: Sell out means everything is gone.
normal.cn: sell out 意为全部售罄。

normal.en: Sale is the noun, sell is the verb.
normal.cn: sale 是名词，sell 是动词。

normal.en: Ads sell products and also ideas.
normal.cn: 广告既卖产品，也卖理念。

abstract.en: To sell is to agree on what a thing is worth.
abstract.cn: 出售，就是就一件东西的价值达成一致。

abstract.en: What sells easily is not always what lasts.
abstract.cn: 好卖的东西未必长久。

abstract.en: A price is a story both sides accept.
abstract.cn: 价格是买卖双方都接受的一个故事。

examples.en: He sold his old bike.
The book sold a million copies.
examples.cn: 这本书卖出了上百万册。

examples.en: They sell fresh vegetables every morning.
examples.cn: 他们每天早上卖新鲜蔬菜。

dict_mnemonic.text: sell 是日耳曼语本族动词，过去式 sold、过去分词 sold，名词形式为 sale，另有 seller 等派生词。

root: 源自古英语 sellan（给予、交出），属日耳曼语本族词，核心义「交出去换取报偿」。

sensesIntro.en: Sell means to exchange for money, to persuade buyers, or to be bought.
sensesIntro.cn: sell 意为出售、推销或卖得如何。

core.en: To hand something over and receive money.
core.cn: 把东西交出去，换回钱。

branches.en: Goods go to a buyer for cash.
branches.cn: 货物换钱交到买家手里。

branches.en: A pitch makes a product attractive.
branches.cn: 一番说辞让产品显得诱人。

branches.en: Numbers show how well goods move.
branches.cn: 数字显示货物卖得如何。

branches.en: Every sale joins a seller and a buyer.
branches.cn: 每笔买卖都连接着卖家与买家。

branches.en: Persuasion is part of the modern sale.
branches.cn: 说服是现代销售的一部分。

intro.en: Sell has a small but very common family of sales words.
intro.cn: sell 的派生词不多，但 sales 相关词非常常用。

latinIntro.en: This is a Germanic word, so there are no Latin base forms to add.
latinIntro.cn: 这是日耳曼语词，没有对应的拉丁语词根条目。

items.example: They sell fruit at the market.

items.meaning: a product that sells very well
an event with no tickets left

definition_en: to make something go to another place or person, to mail, to order someone to go, or to pass on a message
core_image: 一封写好的信被投入邮筒，落下去时轻轻一响
scene: 她把邮件发送给了所有同事。She sent the email to all her colleagues.
sceneCN: 这里 sent 是「发送」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把邮件发送给了所有同事。

senses.title: Send a message
senses.definition: to make a message or signal go to someone
senses.definitionCN: 使信息或信号到达某人那里
senses.example: She sent the email to all her colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 她把邮件发送给了所有同事。
senses.why: This is the everyday communication sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常通讯义。

senses.title: Mail something
senses.definition: to mail a letter or parcel
senses.definitionCN: 邮寄信件或包裹
senses.example: I sent the parcel yesterday.
senses.why: Mail is a physical kind of sending.
senses.whyCN: 邮寄是实物形式的发送。

senses.title: Dispatch a person
senses.definition: to order someone to go somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 命令某人前往某处
senses.example: They sent a doctor to the village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们派了一名医生去村里。
senses.why: People can be sent as well as things.
senses.whyCN: 人也能像物品一样被派出去。

senses.title: Convey a feeling
senses.definition: to cause a feeling or idea to reach others
senses.definitionCN: 使情感或想法传达到他人那里
senses.example: The music sent a shiver through the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐让整个人群打了个寒战。
senses.why: Sending can be emotional rather than physical.
senses.whyCN: 发送可以是情感上的而非物理的。

intro.en: Send comes from Old English sendan, to cause to go.
intro.cn: send 源自古英语 sendan（使前往）。

items.en: Sendan meant to cause someone or something to go.
items.cn: sendan 意为使人或物前往。

items.en: The past form sende became sent.
items.cn: 过去式 sende 演变为 sent。

items.en: Senden covered letters, people, and gifts.
items.cn: senden 涵盖信件、人与礼物。

items.en: Send extends to messages and signals.
items.cn: send 扩展到信息与信号。

items.en: Send for means to ask someone to come.
items.cn: send for 意为请某人前来。

note.en: Send is compared with similar-looking words and with words for passing things on.
note.cn: 把 send 与形近词以及表示传递的词作比较。

entries.definition: to bring something to a place

normalIntro.en: Send means to make something or someone go from here to there.
normalIntro.cn: send 意为使某物或某人从这里去到那里。

normal.en: Send has the irregular past sent.
normal.cn: send 的不规则过去式是 sent。

normal.en: You send an email, but you send for a doctor.
normal.cn: 你发送邮件，但派人去请医生用 send for。

normal.en: The sender signs the parcel.
normal.cn: 寄件人在包裹上签名。

normal.en: Send out means to mail many things.
normal.cn: send out 意为寄出许多东西。

normal.en: A send-off is a farewell party.
normal.cn: send-off 是一场送别会。

abstract.en: A message leaves the hand but keeps the sender inside it.
abstract.cn: 信息离开手，却把发送者留在其中。

abstract.en: Distance is what sending tries to defeat.
abstract.cn: 距离正是发送想要战胜的东西。

abstract.en: To send a person is to trust the road.
abstract.cn: 派一个人出去，就是把路交给他信任。

examples.en: She sent the email to all her colleagues.
examples.cn: 她把邮件发送给了所有同事。

examples.en: I sent the parcel yesterday.
They sent a doctor to the village.
examples.cn: 他们派了一名医生去村里。

dict_mnemonic.text: send 源自古英语 sendan（使前往），本义「使人或物出发」，后扩展为发送信息、邮寄与派遣。

root: 源自古英语 sendan（使前往），核心义「使某物从一处去到另一处」。

sensesIntro.en: Send means to transmit a message, mail something, dispatch a person, or convey a feeling.

core.en: Causing something to travel to another place.
core.cn: 使某物前往另一处。

branches.en: A message leaving for its reader.
branches.cn: 一条奔向读者的信息。

branches.en: A letter or parcel on its way.
branches.cn: 在路上的信件或包裹。

branches.en: A person ordered to travel.
branches.cn: 被派上路的人。

branches.en: A feeling passed into a crowd.
branches.cn: 传进人群的情绪。

branches.en: Words and parcels travel by one verb.
branches.cn: 文字与包裹共用一个动词。

intro.en: Send belongs to the old Germanic family of going and causing to go.
intro.cn: send 属于日耳曼语中表示「去」与「使去」的古老词族。

items.example: They sent the goods by train.
They gave him a warm send-off.
The package is sendable by post.

definition_zh: 年长的；高级的；前辈；毕业班学生
definition_en: older, higher in rank, a person of greater age or rank, or a student in the final year
core_image: 会议桌一端坐着资历最深的人，所有人都先等他开口
scene: 她比办公室里的其他人都年长。She is senior to everyone else in the office.
sceneCN: 这里 senior 是「年长的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她比办公室里的其他人都年长。

senses.title: Older
senses.definition: older than another person
senses.definitionCN: 比另一个人年长
senses.example: She is senior to everyone else in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 她比办公室里的其他人都年长。
senses.why: This is the basic age sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的年龄义。

senses.title: Higher in rank
senses.definition: higher in rank or position
senses.definitionCN: 级别或职位更高
senses.example: He holds a senior position in the company.
senses.exampleCN: 他在公司担任高级职位。
senses.why: Age and rank often go together.
senses.whyCN: 年龄与级别常常相连。

senses.title: An elder
senses.definition: a person older or higher in rank than another
senses.definitionCN: 比另一人年长或级别更高的人
senses.example: She learned the trade from her seniors.
senses.exampleCN: 她从前辈那里学会了这门手艺。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the person.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为指人的名词。

senses.title: Final-year student
senses.definition: a student in the last year of school or college
senses.definitionCN: 中学或大学的最后一年级学生
senses.example: The seniors are planning their graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业班学生正在筹划毕业典礼。
senses.why: The oldest students are called seniors.
senses.whyCN: 年级最高的学生被称为毕业班学生。

intro.en: Senior is Latin for older, the comparative of senex, old man.
intro.cn: senior 是拉丁语中「更年长的」，是 senex（老人）的比较级。

items.en: Senex meant old man.
items.cn: senex 意为老人。

items.en: Senior meant older.
items.cn: senior 意为更年长的。

items.en: Seignor meant lord or elder.
items.cn: seignor 意为领主或长者。

items.en: Senior entered English as a title of rank.
items.cn: senior 作为表示级别的称谓进入英语。

items.en: It now also marks the final school year.
items.cn: 现在它也指学校的最后一年级。

note.en: Senior is compared with similar-looking words and with words for age and rank.
note.cn: 把 senior 与形近词以及表示年龄与级别的词作比较。

entries.definition: rank gained by length of service

normalIntro.en: Senior means older or higher, and the oldest students are seniors.
normalIntro.cn: senior 意为年长或级别更高，最年长的学生也叫毕业班学生。

normal.en: Senior is the comparative of senex.
normal.cn: senior 是 senex 的比较级。

normal.en: A senior manager outranks a junior one.
normal.cn: 高级经理的级别高于初级经理。

normal.en: Senior citizens often get discounts.
normal.cn: 老年人常常享受折扣。

normal.en: She is senior to me by five years.
normal.cn: 她比我年长五岁。

normal.en: Senior year is the final year of school.
normal.cn: 毕业班学年是学校的最后一年。

abstract.en: Time gives one kind of rank; work gives another.
abstract.cn: 时间给人一种是资历，工作给人另一种。

abstract.en: A senior is someone who has already walked the road.
abstract.cn: 前辈是已经走过这条路的人。

abstract.en: The last year in school is also the first step out.
abstract.cn: 学校的最后一年，也是走出去的第一步。

examples.en: She is senior to everyone else in the office.
examples.cn: 她比办公室里的其他人都年长。

examples.en: He holds a senior position in the company.
examples.cn: 他在公司担任高级职位。

examples.en: The seniors are planning their graduation.
examples.cn: 毕业班学生正在筹划毕业典礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: senior 是拉丁语 senex（老人）的比较级，本义「更年长的」，后引申为级别更高者与毕业班学生。

root: 源自拉丁语 senex（老人）的比较级 senior，核心义「更年长、地位更高」。

sensesIntro.en: Senior means older, higher in rank, an elder, or a final-year student.
sensesIntro.cn: senior 意为年长的、高级的、前辈或毕业班学生。

core.en: Ahead in years or in rank.
core.cn: 在年岁或级别上更靠前。

branches.en: The older of two people.
branches.cn: 两人中年长的一位。

branches.en: A higher place in a hierarchy.
branches.cn: 等级体系中更高的位置。

branches.en: A person who has gone before.
branches.cn: 先走过一段路的人。

branches.en: The oldest class in a school.
branches.cn: 学校里年级最高的班级。

branches.en: Age and rank share one comparison.
branches.cn: 年龄与级别共用一个比较形式。

intro.en: Senior belongs to the Latin senex family of age and rank.
intro.cn: senior 属于拉丁语 senex（老）词族，关联年龄与级别。

latinIntro.en: Latin senex and its comparative senior are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 senex 及其比较级 senior 是历史词根。

items.example: The seniors welcomed the new staff.
The senator gave a short speech.
